title: The treatment-side signature columns, the operation a signature record arrives on, the event names, the two list codes and the closure are not specified for rwb-treatment
source: Recovery Workbench User Stories Epic 2 Story Files v5, RWB E2 018 E signature flow for customers and the bank v1, sections 11, 12, 13 and 16; Recovery Workbench TSD S2 TDR, settlement and deed in lieu v2, T3.1, T3.2 and T-A.1 to T-A.2; Recovery Workbench FSD S2 TDR, settlement and deed in lieu v3, A2.7 to A2.9; Recovery Workbench Architecture v5 Text Extract v1, slides 13, 18 and 42; context pack S2 (ownership rows of S2: one table, four REST operations, one event, one workflow); Recovery Workbench Microservice Story Template and Rules v1, sections R5.5 and R7.2
section: 3 Preconditions; 4 Flow; 7 Acceptance criteria AC1 to AC8; 8 Business rules; 9 State transitions; 11 Data; 12.2; 12.3; 12.5; 12.6; 12.7; 13 Solution plan; 14 Validation and messages
description: One combined row for the treatment side of legacy RWB-E2-018. (1) TSD S2 T3.1 gives treatment DF-TRT-001 to DF-TRT-033 and only DF-TRT-030 signature_status carries a signature fact; there is no column for the method, the provider reference, the send time, the signed time or the window end, and FSD S2 A2.7 to A2.9 have no field catalog at all. (2) No source names the operation a signature record arrives on: the legacy has the in-process call TreatmentApi.recordSignature(treatmentId, signed, method, at), the ownership rows of S2 carry four operations and none of them is a signature operation, and the plan holds no rwb-treatment contract story for the caller. (3) No source names the event a treatment publishes when a signature is recorded or when the window closes; the catalogue gives rwb-treatment TreatmentApproved and TreatmentClosed, the comms catalogue names only the three notice events, and the legacy raises CUSTOMER_SIGNED and CUSTOMER_ACCEPTED in P3. (4) No source names the list code of the method values E_SIGNATURE, BRANCH and PAPER as the treatment sees them, or the mapping between the legacy request statuses QUEUED, SENT, SIGNED, DECLINED, EXPIRED and LOV-TRT-SIGNATURE with PENDING, SIGNED and NOT_SIGNED. (5) No source names the reason code of a window that closes on validity, the operation names of the reference-data reads, or the activity names the stage runs. (6) No source says who closes the window in the target: the legacy has P3 announce OFFER_EXPIRED and call the signature module, while the treatment's own valid_until and the offer timer are S2's.
evidence: TSD S2 v2 T3.1 (DF-TRT-030 signature_status and no other signature field) and T3.2 (LOV-TRT-SIGNATURE: PENDING, SIGNED, NOT_SIGNED); TSD S2 v2 T-A.1 (API-S2-001 to API-S2-004 only, no signature operation); legacy RWB-E2-018 sections 11, 12 and 13 (DF-DOC-096 to DF-DOC-107 on signature_request; lists for method and request status recorded as additions; no treatment column added); Architecture v5 slide 18 and the comms catalogue on slide 42; context pack S2 ownership rows of S2.
proposed: Add the five nullable signature columns and their two indexes on the service's own Flyway sequence, carry the record on the additive properties of the declared update operation, name the two events after the outcome they carry, read the method and status lists at their version through the reference-data contract, and let the stage's offer-validity timer close the window with one closure callback.

title: Architecture v5 gives S2 to P5 the Temporal cell and no cell from P6 or P5 into S2, while the legacy seam is one synchronous in-process call and the work package lists DP-11
source: Recovery Workbench Architecture v5 Text Extract v1, slide 13 (connection matrix) and slides 8, 11 and 18; Recovery Workbench User Stories Epic 2 Story Files v5, RWB E2 018 E signature flow for customers and the bank v1, sections 4 and 12; Recovery Workbench Microservice Story Template and Rules v1, sections R3, R5.5 DP-11 and R5.7; work package B2-S2-020 story line for RWB-S2-E2018-APP; gap CG-B-P6-04-E2018-3 of the P6 slice
section: 1 Story; 3 Preconditions; 4 Flow; 5 Exception paths; 7 Acceptance criteria AC1, AC4, AC6; 12.1; 12.2; 12.4; 12.5; 12.9; 13 Solution plan; 18 Traceability
description: Two sources give the same seam two transports and two directions. Architecture v5 slide 13 is the full connection matrix: the S2 Treatment row holds T against the P5 Document column, which is a Temporal activity on the owner's queue, and the P6 Comms row holds nothing against S2 while the S2 row holds nothing against P6, so no cell carries the record the legacy writes. Its notes add that route services reach shared capabilities through Temporal, never through REST. The legacy story publishes the seam as an in-process published interface that returns inside the same request: the communications module calls TreatmentApi.recordSignature and the treatment module is told the result. DP-11 turns an in-process published interface into a REST contract with a mock, one hop and a 2 s timeout, the work package names DP-11 in the pattern set, and the Ownership Map already publishes PATCH /treatments/{treatmentId} on the treatment. By the precedence of R3 the architecture catalogue wins, but the catalogue publishes no signature activity on queue rwb-document or rwb-comms for this capability and no inbound cell into S2, so following the matrix literally would leave all three stories with no published shape to build against on Day 1.
evidence: Architecture v5 slide 13 row S2 Treatment holds T in the P5 Document column and nothing in the P6 column, row P6 Comms holds nothing in the S2 column and row P5 Document is empty in the S2 column, with the note that route services reach shared capabilities through Temporal and never through REST; slide 8 lists the call types separately; legacy RWB-E2-018 section 4 step 6 and section 12 publish TreatmentApi.recordSignature as a Java interface; Template and Rules v1 R5.5 DP-11 and R5.7; work package B2-S2-020 story line (patterns DP01, DP05, DP07, DP09, DP10, DP11, DP13, DP15, DP19; all four dependency lists empty).
proposed: Publish the record on the update operation of /api/recovery/treatment/v1 with a fake, so the P6 caller and this service build on the same day, and record that a later move to a Temporal activity changes the client and no criterion of section 7.

title: The legacy one module and one transaction for the signature request, the signed version and the treatment field become three owners, and the offer expiry that closed the request is now the treatment's own date
source: Recovery Workbench User Stories Epic 2 Story Files v5, RWB E2 018 E signature flow for customers and the bank v1, sections 4, 8, 9, 11 and 13; Recovery Workbench TSD S2 TDR, settlement and deed in lieu v2, T3.1 and T4; Recovery Workbench Architecture v5 Text Extract v1, slides 4, 16, 29 and 41; Ownership Map v1; context pack S2 (ownership rows of S2); Recovery Workbench Microservice Story Template and Rules v1, sections R3 and R5.5
section: 1 Story; 2 Business rationale; 3 Preconditions; 7 Acceptance criteria AC3, AC4; 9 State transitions; 11 Data; 12.6; 12.7; 13 Solution plan; 19 Out of scope
description: The legacy key is one module whose data table carries signature_request and whose section 12 publishes the treatment interface, so the request, the signed version and the treatment field were written inside one schema by one team, and the offer expiry reached the signature module as a call from the case. The target splits the same facts three ways - the request and the signed copy with P5 rwb-document, the circuit and the basis with P6 rwb-comms, the treatment and DF-TRT-030 with S2 rwb-treatment - and keeps the offer validity on the treatment. No source states how the three stay consistent, which service is authoritative for the outcome, or who closes an open request when the offer expires; the legacy's single transaction across the request and the treatment write cannot be reproduced across three schemas. This story therefore writes the treatment state itself, treats the request and the signed version as P5 values it never reads, and closes its own window on its own validity so the case hears an outcome rather than an intent.
evidence: Legacy RWB-E2-018 section 11 lists DF-DOC-096 to DF-DOC-107 for signature_request beside DF-TRT-030 written through the treatment interface, section 9 has P3 make the case change, and section 4 step 9 has P3 announce OFFER_EXPIRED and call SignatureApi.cancel; Architecture v5 slide 41 places documents and the signature request with P5 rwb-document and templates with P6 rwb-comms; TSD S2 T3.1 carries DF-TRT-010 valid_until and DF-TRT-030; Ownership Map v1 and the context pack S2 give the treatment table to S2.
proposed: Let rwb-treatment own the signature record of its own treatment and the closure of its own window, let rwb-document own the request, its statuses and the signed version, let rwb-comms own the basis and the circuit, and reconcile the three on the published operation and the two events rather than on a shared table.
